chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, Most High, support him—informed me of: from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān and Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said:

I performed wudu (ablution) for Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام at Jamʿ, and he had urinated. So I handed him water and he performed istinjāʾ, then I poured for him a palmful, and he washed his face; and a palmful with which he washed his right forearm; and a palmful with which he washed his left forearm; then he wiped his head and his feet with the remaining moisture.

key_terms.فَضْلِ النَّدَى: the remaining moisture left on the hand
key_terms.كَفًّا: a palmful or handful of water

ai.seo_question: How did Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام perform wudu (ablution) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the manner of the wudu (ablution) of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام after relieving himself. It depicts a concise form of wudu (ablution): washing the face and both forearms with measured handfuls of water, then wiping the head and feet with remaining moisture.
